steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM (mandatory): unit tests for new pure logic MUST be property-based (proptest) with state-delta discipline where state mutates; single-example unit tests are FALLBACK only with a # bypass: comment. Acceptance scenarios are the cucumber .feature file (already authored by DISTILL — un-pend, do not re-author). Integration/browser tests stay single-example — they verify wiring. The pure logic of this step is SQL (the verdict function); its property test is the DISTILL bulk parity (TestRunner over the DDD-16 alphabet, >= 10k names per run, batches of 1,000 through unnest WITH ORDINALITY), already authored — un-ignore, do not re-author; OQ-D4 is settled by the scaffold (a seeded TestRunner loop). Contract shapes: verdict function pure (return-only, IMMUTABLE); enforce trigger a guard (returns NEW unchanged or raises; mutation set empty); seed_row_predating_name_rule bounded-change {the one caller row; the two triggers' enable state, restored before commit}. WHY THE SEAM LANDS WITH 0019: the moment 0019 exists every scenario schema refuses the raw F1/F2 legacy inserts, so the migration, the seam and the fixture switch must be one commit to keep the default lane green; the seam cannot precede 0019 (it disables triggers by name). The seam runs on the scenario's own pool and schema (the acceptance harness gives each scenario one); the ALTER is transactional and serialised by its lock, so no concurrent scenario sees its rule absent (DDD-10; C7c). Never log names: the trigger's MESSAGE, HINT and the seam's error carry the table and arm, never the row's name (no DETAIL row dump, DDD-4; D14 of the precedents). Migration immutability: sqlx checksums freeze a migration file once a database has applied it, and dev auto-deploys from main, so 0019 may be edited freely until the slice is pushed and never after; finish the self-check before pushing. Do NOT add a Store::probe check for the triggers (DDD-9: the documented undo would become an outage). Named faults killed here: \s / [[:space:]] / btrim(name) / regex trim instead of the 25-point set (parity exact pairs); a stricter arm (any Cf refused, octet_length) or a looser one (off-by-one U+007F-009F, 2028-202E, 2066-2069 bounds); precedence reordered; a non-IMMUTABLE verdict; no encoding guard. Lessons: write invisible characters as escapes, never as literals (raw strings in Rust, U& or E'' escapes in SQL); seed fixtures before any universe snapshot; acceptance runs the prebuilt foundry binary, so rebuild + warm before every lane; bound every lane with timeout and clear leftover containers if a run is killed; another session may share this worktree, so check for running lanes and containers first. MUTATION: cargo-mutants cannot mutate SQL. The Rust surface (name_rule_legacy_seam.rs) gets >= 80% (timeout 1800 cargo mutants --in-diff <step diff> --file crates/foundry-store/src/name_rule_legacy_seam.rs; its kill test is the seam store test un-ignored in 02-01, so record this step's survivors and re-run there). The SQL arms are pinned instead by the bulk parity (arm-exact) plus the exact boundary pairs, the self-check drift test (02-01) and the SQL_ASCII test; additionally hand-mutate a scratch copy of 0019 once per arm class (each range bound +/-1, one White_Space point dropped, precedence swapped, WHEN dropped, OF name dropped) and confirm a named test goes red, recording the table in the mutation report (03-02).
